text:
maria: quick idea — let's prototype a lightweight 'checkout' flow for runtime overrides (routing / quotas). validate -> canary -> approval -> apply. goal: surface risk early and make rollbacks trivial.

alex: +1. checklist: scope semantics, TTLs, auto-approve thresholds, canary samples, and clear audit trail. keep path simple for single-tenant tweaks.

tess: console UX thought: a 3-step modal: Details (who/why/diff), Safety checks (automated warnings + canary config), Approvers (list + approve buttons). show cost delta and affected routes inline. small banner on config page for pending checkouts.

jun: rough API sketch:
```http
POST /v1/overrides/checkout
Host: api.redwood.internal
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "config_id": "route:primary",
  "scope": {"tenants": ["t1"], "percent": 0.05},
  "diff": [{"path": "route_weight", "from": 0.6, "to": 0.5}],
  "canary": {"sample_percent": 1, "duration_minutes": 15},
  "ttl_seconds": 3600,
  "requester": "maria",
  "reason": "reduce latency spike",
  "notify_channels": ["#eng-platform"]
}
```
Response should include checkout_id and validation warnings. UI shows warnings inline.

sahil: telemetry: emit checkout.start (checkout_id, requester, diff), checkout.canary.metrics (pre/post snapshot for canary), checkout.apply. Tag traffic with checkout_id when applied. capture per-tenant qps/latency/error and compute deltas. ops alert if error delta > 5% or p50 up > 25% during canary window.

ops-bot: autosafety rule: if canary sees >5% error delta in 10m, auto-fail and revert the checkout. will post details + revert link to #incidents and ping on-call.

kevin: approval fatigue risk. propose auto-approve when: tenants.length <= 2 AND percent <= 0.01 AND absolute quota change < 10%. otherwise require at least one approver. special-case: any change touching names ["primary","fallback"] needs manual approval.

maria: agree on special-case. also default TTL 24h for quick reversions; allow extensions but require re-approval if extension > 7d. approver must add a short note.

tess: UX nit: on the approve modal show a one-click rollback command (cli snippet) and the estimated revert impact. also add an 'escalate to on-call' option for urgent approvals.

jun: implementation plan: small checkout service that stores pending checkouts, runs safety checks, triggers canary router rules, and transitions states. POC next week.

alex: i'll draft a short RFC + API contract. include storage model: checkout object + history entries for apply/revert/extensions.

sahil: also keep an extension history and who extended. telemetry owners: me.

maria: decision items to capture in RFC: auto-approve thresholds, default TTL and extension policy, canary sizing & duration defaults, autosafety thresholds, API shape, console flows, telemetry events. owners: @alex api, @tess console, @sahil telemetry, @jun ops.

kevin: sgtm :+1:

maria: leaving this open 24h for quick comments, then i'll file the RFC and tag owners.

ops-bot: reminder — include a test plan for simulated canary failures and an incident playbook link in RFC.

maria: good call, adding to RFC checklist. thanks everyone!
